(Vault 31er 3) That's not how it works, doorknob.|Vault 31 dwellers protesting after hearing of Bud Askins' death}} The '''Vault 31 dwellers''', also called '''Vault 31ers''',Referred to as such in the subtitles of "[[The Golden Rule]]" are the residents of [[Vault 31]] {{In|FOTV}}. This refers to both the occupants of the vault in general, as well as the specific group of 31ers who are reactivated by [[Norm MacLean]]. ==Background== ===Bud's Buds=== {{Main|Bud's Buds}} The occupants of Vault 31 are all pre-[[Great War|War]] [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] junior employees who were selected to join [[Bud Askins]]' experimental management training program, "[[Bud's Buds]]." At least some of them were selected from recent [[Vault-Tec University]] graduates.[[Bud's Buds!]] The intention behind this program, as planned by Askins, was to achieve an "absolute monopoly" in Vault-Tec corporate strategy by physically outliving all competitors. Bud's vision culminated in the [[Three Vaults]] (Vaults 31, [[Vault 32|32]], and [[Vault 33|33]]). Vault 31 contained only cryostasis chambers where members of Bud's Buds would be preserved, while Vaults 32 and 33 would contain actual civilian populations (also hand-picked by Bud and his team for genetically desirable traits). Every thirty years,[[Bud Askins]]: ''"No, no, no. They're supposed to come out once every thirty years. This isn't even a cogent plan. It's just chaos."''
("[[The Innovator]]") or as needed, a member of Bud's Buds would be awakened from their pod and released from Vault 31 into the population of the other two connected vaults, who had all been taught that Vault 31 was also a normal, populated Vault just like theirs. The Buds would find a way to become the overseers of Vaults 32 and 33 and use their positions to indoctrinate their dwellers into model Vault-Tec citizens. The ultimate goal was to breed a generation of "super-managers" from Bud's original Vault-Tec trainee staff, who would go on to claim the post-War world as their own.[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"So what's Vault 32 and 33? Just people to be controlled?"''
[[Bud Askins]]: ''"What? No! When you put it like that, it sounds downright morally questionable. They're our breeding pool, the ultimate expression of HR R&D. Genetically selected to breed with my Buds to create a class of super managers. People with positivity, people who make lemonade. People who will inherit the Earth after we've wiped the surface clean."''
("[[The Beginning]]") When the stage was finally set, with all competition on the surface eliminated, any remaining Vault 31 dwellers would also be reactivated and released onto the surface along with the other Vaults' indoctrinated populations, to reclaim the surface for Vault-Tec on [[Reclamation Day (event)|Reclamation Day]]. Following this, the 31ers were to contact Vault-Tec's "investors" to start Phase 2 of their plans, although it is unclear how much of Phase 2 the dwellers were made aware of, or whether they knew that these "investors" were actually the [[Enclave]].[[Ronnie McCurtry|Ronnie]]: ''"Hey, boss. Now that we've found food, it's time for phase two?"''
[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"What is your name?"''
Ronnie: ''"Oh, um, I'm Ronnie. McCurtry."''
Norm MacLean: ''"I decide the next steps up here, Ronnie."''
Ronnie: ''"I know, yeah, you're the-- you're the boss. I know you call the shots. Just thought I'd introduce myself, 'cause I was Bud's personal assistant."''
Norm MacLean: ''"Hm, so?"''
Ronnie: ''"So, uh, let's just say I was the guy who took the lunch orders when Bud was meeting with the Vault investors. 'Future Enterprise Ventures'? The whole plan for Vaults 32 and 33?"''
Norm MacLean: ''"What do you know about that?"''
Ronnie: ''"Like I said, I was just the guy who got the lunch orders, but I do know that Phase 2 was very important to the experiment."''
({{FOTV|2|4}})[[Ronnie McCurtry]]: ''"Alright. Comms Room. Clark, Pete, with me. (switches clicking) It's dead."''
[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"Who were you hoping to contact?"''
Ronnie: ''"The investors. [...] Hey, Clark, you're project manager. Get this operational, stat."''
[[Clark (TV series)|Clark]]: ''"Shouldn't take long."''
Ronnie: ''"Hey, Pete, go try that one."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) Most of the junior employees chosen for the program fully believed in Bud Askins and Vault-Tec's plans to the point of utter, unshakeable loyalty; one of the only exceptions was [[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]], who joined Vault-Tec only a week before the Great War and thus was never exposed to the company as much as the others were.Claudia: ''"Who even are you, seriously?"''
[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"I'm the product of 200 years of genetic engineering. Part of a race of super managers. And all of you have been selected to be my staff. You think we've been left locked in Vault 31 by accident? You think Bud Askins made mistakes?"''
[[Clark (TV series)|Clark]]: ''"Never."''
[[Pete (TV series)|Pete]]: ''"No chance."''
Claudia: ''"Well..."''
Clark: ''"Oh, my God, Claudia, we're trying to have a conversation here."''
({{FOTV|2|2}}) They were adherents of Vault-Tec's corporate culture and competent workers when given delegated tasks, but were not independent thinkers and easily conformed to instructions from any claimed Vault-Tec authority.[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"This is Bud's final test. If I can lead you all to finding our way out of here, we'll have proven ourselves worthy to carry on Vault-Tec's corporate strategy together. And those of you who work quickly and as a team... will receive these merit dots."''
[[Vault 31 dweller|Vault 31er]]: ''"Ooh!"''
[[Clark (TV series)|Clark]]: ''"Merit dots?"''
Claudia: ''"Oh."''
Clark: ''"Wait. I took notes at a meeting with the company that installed ventilation. Dibs on ventilation!"''
Claudia: ''"Oh, the fire suppression system. Maybe we can get some water from there."''
Vault 31er 1: ''"Maybe we could borrow{{sic}} underground, make a tunnel."''
Vault 31er 2: ''"I'll hack the Overseer's console, so we can override some security protocols."''
Vault 31er 3: ''"There has to be a schematics{{sic}} somewhere around here…"''
({{FOTV|2|2}}) Their faith (and lack of independent thinking) was so ingrained that any revelation of things going awry was enough to throw them into disarray;Vault 31er: ''"Where's Bud Askins? Has anyone seen Bud Askins?"''
[[Clark (TV series)|Clark]]: ''"I'm sorry, why are we all here? I thought this was gonna be more of a one-by-one situation."''
[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"There's been a change of plan."''
[[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]]: ''"Should I be able to see by now?"''
Clark: ''"Relax, Claudia. There's been a change of plans, obviously. Jeez."''
[[Executive assistant]]: ''"(screaming)"''
Claudia: ''"Is she good?"''
Executive assistant: ''"I'm okay."''
Norm: ''"Everyone, if I can just try and explain."''
Claudia: ''"If they thawed everyone at once, that must mean it's Reclamation Day."''
Norm: ''"About that. It's been 200 years since you were frozen. It is Reclamation Day. But unfortunately, Bud Askins is, uh... uh... [...] Bud Askins is dead."''
Claudia: ''"What?"''
[[Pete (TV series)|Pete]]: ''"Oh, no."''
Norm: ''"So, if we can just try and remain calm. We need to figure out a way to get out of here, together."''
Clark: ''"'Get out of here'? Wait, wait, wait. You're saying we're trapped?"''
[[Ronnie McCurtry]]: ''"Is there someone else that we can speak to about this?"''
Vault 31ers: ''"(panicked chatter) (exclaiming)"''
Norm: ''"Please. Please no."''
Vault 31er: ''"Oh, God."''
Vault 31er: ''"I can't believe this."''
Pete: ''"Everyone! I'm just gonna go back. Could someone help me go back, please?"''
Norm: ''"Um, if we could just try and stay focused."''
Claudia: ''"Uh, someone ate all the crackers from my welcoming kit."''
Clark: ''"We're all gonna die. We're all gonna die."''
({{FOTV|2|2}}) on the other hand, this also made them dangerous, because they were willing to kill to make sure that these plans succeeded.[[Ronnie McCurtry]]: ''"Don't worry."''
Claudia: ''"Ronnie!"''
Ronnie: ''"We'll give him a fair trial."''
Claudia: ''"Stop! No, don't!"''
Ronnie: ''"This is America, after all."''
Claudia: ''"Stop! What are you gonna do to him?"''
Ronnie: ''"You're not one of us either, Claudia. You only got this job last week."''
({{FOTV|2|8}})[[Ronnie McCurtry]]: ''"He's not one of us. He's been lying to us this entire time."''
[[Clark (TV series)|Clark]]: ''"So, what do we do with him?"''
[[Pete (TV series)|Pete]]: ''"He's dangerous. Untrustworthy."''
Ronnie: ''"Right, right. And if we let him go, he could come back and try and kill us."''
Clark: ''"Yeah."''
Ronnie: ''"Right? Wait, I'm actually pretty sure that the Vault-Tec Handbook says that impersonating management is punishable by death."''
Clark: ''"Oh, well, if you're pretty sure the Vault-Tec Handbook says that, I mean..."''
Pete: ''"And if, you know, if that's protocol."''
Clark: ''"Yeah. Yeah."''
Pete: ''"Right?"''
({{FOTV|2|7}}) ===Post-War experimental operation=== On the day of the Great War, Bud's plan went into motion. The members of his program were all put into cryonic preservation inside Vault 31,{{FOTV|1|8}}: The date on Hank's cryo chamber lists him as having been frozen on October 23, 2077. As seen later in "[[The Golden Rule]]," this entry date also appears on other cryo chambers. while Bud himself was preserved in a rudimentary "[[rollerbrain]]" to act as Vault 31's overseer. In this role, he would oversee his trainees' release and integration into Vaults 32 and 33 over time. The experimental process continued seemingly according to plan overall for the next 219 years. Over this period, twenty of the Vault 31 dwellers were reactivated at one time or another and sent into the neighboring Vaults to take power as overseer and carry out their Vault-Tec plans.{{FOTV|1|8}}: The hall Norm enters shows the underground cryo storage lined with banks of cryo-vats. There are 9 chambers per bank on each side, with at least 7 pairs of banks visible. 7*2*9=126. As seen in the episode, two full banks on the right are empty, as well as two additional chambers in a further bank, making up 20 occupants released. By 2296, three of the trainees were active in Vault 33 ([[Betty Pearson]], [[Steph Harper]], and the current overseer, [[Hank MacLean]]), while at least one had been active in Vault 32 ([[Ian Jackson]], its incumbent overseer) prior to 2294; around that time, the Vault 32 dwellers apparently discovered the truth behind the Three Vaults, and they may have also suffered a resource shortage from overpopulation; whatever the case, the entire Vault's population ended up perishing in an internal conflict. ===Norm MacLean's intervention=== The collapse of Vault 32, followed by an attack on Vault 33 by [[Vault 32 raider|raiders posing as Vault 32 dwellers]] in 2296, would end up throwing a wrench in Bud's plans. Around July that year, Hank's son, [[Norm MacLean]], entered Vault 31 and discovered the truth behind Bud's Buds. Bud locked him into the Vault, intending to silence him either through death or coercing him into entering a cryopod, but this went awry. Norm sabotaged the inter-Vault communications, preventing Bud and his Buds in the other Vaults from interacting,{{FOTV|2|1}} and incapacitated (if not killed) Bud by damaging his robotic body. He simultaneously released at least 21 of the frozen employees, convincing them that he was their new leader after Bud's untimely demise. After gaining their obedience, he then relied on their knowledge of Vault 31 to escape to the surface through a ventilation shaft, claiming to be leading them for Reclamation Day.{{FOTV|2|2}} After they entered the urban Los Angeles ruins and secured food supplies, [[Ronnie McCurtry]] effectively took charge over Norm and led the group to the former Vault-Tec headquarters to continue Phase 2 of Bud Askins' and the Vault investors' plans. Aside from Claudia, most of the Vault 31ers seemed apathetic towards the devastation around them, with Ronnie, [[Clark (TV series)|Clark]], and [[Pete (TV series)|Pete]] acting particularly callous. Inside the headquarters, Ronnie directed the group to try and make contact with Vault-Tec's "investors," but he soon discovered that Norm had been lying to them about being Bud's successor; Ronnie then called for Norm to be executed, which the 31ers went along with. Claudia disagreed and tried to help Norm, inadvertently releasing a swarm of [[Radroach (TV series)|radroaches]] inside an elevator shaft which promptly attacked the 31ers. Most of the 31ers were maimed or killed by the radroaches, with only Claudia and Norm confirmed to have survived. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== ====[[The Beginning]]==== During this episode, [[Norm MacLean]] first discovers the truth behind Vault 31, seeing the many Vault 31 dwellers dormant inside their cryo chambers. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Innovator]]==== The Vault 31 dwellers remain dormant inside their cryo chambers, but Norm formulates an escape plan; he primes a number of the cryo chambers for reactivation, banking on using their occupants' knowledge of the vault to escape, fending off Bud, who tries to stop him, ineffectually. ====[[The Golden Rule]]==== {{section|FOTV}} ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== {{section|FOTV}} ====[[The Wrangler]]==== {{section|FOTV}} ====[[The Handoff]]==== {{section|FOTV}} ====[[The Strip]]==== As the dwellers drag [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] through [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|headquarters]], [[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]] protests, causing [[Ronnie McCurtry]] to throw her against the wall, inadvertently hitting an elevator button. When the doors open, [[Radroach (TV series)|radroaches]] emerge from the elevator shaft and slaughter the Vault 31 dwellers. Only Norm and the injured Claudia survive. ==Known members== In total, there were at least 126 dwellers inside Vault 31 at the start, based on the number of cryo chambers seen inside the Vault. Twenty dwellers were released as part of the regular experiment, while around 22 dwellers were released by Norm MacLean in July 2296,{{FOTV|2|2}}: At time stamp 25:10, 21 reactivated Vault 31 dwellers can be seen, not including [[Ronnie McCurtry]]. Additionally, eighteen cryo chambers are seen as newly empty. leaving at least 84 dwellers still frozen inside the Vault. ===Norm's group=== In July 2296, Norm released a group of 22 Vault 31 dwellers who have since escaped the Vault with him. Of these, five dwellers' names are known, and can be definitively mapped to members of the group based on their appearance in "[[The Golden Rule]]." Another eight dwellers' names are known due to being on cryo chambers that are emptied during "The Golden Rule," but they cannot currently be mapped to a corresponding dweller seen in the episode.{{Ref|(Note 1)}} ;Names and faces confirmed {{Columns|2| * [[Chloe Glass]]{{Ref|(Note 2)}} * [[Clark (TV series)|Clark]] * [[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]]{{Ref|(Note 1)}} * [[Pete (TV series)|Pete]] * [[Ronnie McCurtry]] }} ;Names known {{Columns|3| * [[Archibald Sachs]]{{FOTV|2|1}}: Name seen at 45:08 on a defreezing cryo chamber; same chamber is empty in "[[The Golden Rule]]." * [[Casey Schulz]]{{FOTV|2|2}}: Not personally identified, but name seen on an empty cryo chamber which was still frozen in previous episodes. * [[Francesca Mahajan]] * [[Joan Polansky]] * [[Joanne Wormwood]]{{Ref|(Note 1)}} * [[Joseph Moerder]] * [[Kathryn Cep]] * [[Thomas Hamilton]] }} ===Dormant dwellers=== The following dwellers' names are known, but it is not known if they are among the dwellers reactivated by Norm. Unless confirmed otherwise, they will be listed as still dormant. {{Columns|3| * [[Elmer Greene]] * [[Chase Powell]] * [[Victoria Alexander]] * [[Christyn Mari]] * [[Arthur Wormeley]] * [[March Sherwood]] * [[Maximillian Dottino]] * [[Tatyana Lee]] * [[Claire Feldman]] }} ==Notes== * {{Note|(Note 1)}} This estimate may be complicated, as Claudia appears to have exited from the cryo chamber that had the name Joanne Wormwood on it. When Claudia is first released, she is seen in a chamber in the middle of one set of three on the bottom left row from the cryo bay entrance, and the second set of newly-opened cryo chambers on the bottom row can also be seen in the distance behind her. This means that she must have been in the second chamber on the bottom left from the entrance, which is exactly the one that had Joanne Wormwood's name on it. * {{Note|(Note 2)}} This character is credited as the "executive assistant" in the cast of "The Golden Rule." They can be mapped together, as the assistant is seen falling out of a pod above and adjacent to the one which was occupied by Claudia. ==Appearances== The Vault 31 dwellers appear {{In|FOTV}}; the group unfrozen by Norm first appears in the TV series' [[Fallout TV series season 2|second season]]. {{FOTV appearances|8=108|9=201|10=202|12=204|13=205|15=207|16=208}} ==Behind the scenes== Among the unnamed characters in Norm's group, one Vault 31er, who can be identified as Chloe Glass from her cryo chamber, is played by stunt performer [[Sydney Olson]], credited as an "executive assistant."
